verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack 3 charges of An Acquired Taste and Devour you after a dive; you win if you stun and all-in before his kit is online.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench's Q (Tongue Lash) has a 7-5s cooldown depending on rank and stacks An Acquired Taste on hit, consuming three stacks for a stun and unlocking Devour (R, 0s cooldown) — that's his only real lane threat, and it's slow to build. Irelia wins short trades with E (Flawless Duet) stun into Q (Bladesurge) reset and Ionian Fervor attack-speed stacks before he can land three Q's. The 47.3% head-to-head over 131 games against a 50% baseline says the lane lead doesn't carry — his health-scaling passive damage and R peel for teammates let him matter late even after losing early exchanges.

tell.watch: His Acquired Taste stacks on you

theirWindow.when: Q lands at 3 stacks on you
theirWindow.what: The third stack of An Acquired Taste turns his next Tongue Lash hit into a stun instead of a slow, and at level 6+ he can immediately Devour (R) you for magic damage with zero cooldown. Back off and let a stack fall rather than trading face-to-face once you're at two.

yourWindow.when: His Q (Tongue Lash) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With his only poke/sustain tool down, step in with E (Flawless Duet) to stun and Mark him, then Q (Bladesurge) onto the Mark to refresh its cooldown and chain autos while Ionian Fervor stacks give you bonus attack speed. He has no slow or shield up to answer it.

start.why: The highest-pick-rate start (89.8% pick, 46.2% WR over 158 games) — the extra HP and lifesteal buy you trades into his Q poke and keep you healthy through the levels before E comes online.

boots.why: 47% WR over 100 games at 60.6% pick — tenacity cuts the duration of his Q-stack stun and the knockup from his W (Abyssal Dive), and magic resist blunts his magic-damage kit.

core.why: Current-HP damage and the slow punish his high-health passive (An Acquired Taste scales off his total health) directly.
Matches the top measured path (50% WR over 32 games, 24.1% pick) and adds the sustained-fight pressure you need since he out-scales raw stat checks late.
Magic resist stacks against his magic-damage Q/W/R while the on-hit magic damage keeps building Ionian Fervor stacks.

situational.when: you need more survivability against his magic burst and Devour
you're ahead and want to snowball dueling pressure instead of sustain
the game runs long and his health-scaling damage starts outpacing your resistances

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping adaptive damage and healing rewards exactly the extended-trade pattern this matchup calls for — stay on him through the stun-reset chain and Conqueror keeps scaling while his Q is down.

summoners.why: The dominant pick (48.4% WR at 81% pick rate) over Flash+Teleport (36.4% WR, 11.6%) — Ignite punishes his Devour all-in by denying the healing his kit relies on and secures kills before he can disengage.

playing.title: Trade only when his Q is down
playing.detail: Tongue Lash is his only poke and sustain tool (7-5s cooldown by rank). Step into exchanges right after he throws and misses, or right after it lands and goes on cooldown.

playing.title: Track his stacks on you, not just his HP
playing.detail: Every Q and auto he lands builds An Acquired Taste. At 3 stacks his next Q stuns you and unlocks Devour (R) at level 6+ — disengage before you hit that third stack.

playing.title: Stun him before he can Abyssal Dive
playing.detail: His W lets him dive down and reappear elsewhere with a knockup, which doubles as an escape. Land E (Flawless Duet) on him before he commits to W so he can't just dive away from your all-in.

playing.title: Chain Q resets off your own E mark
playing.detail: Flawless Duet damages, stuns, and Marks anyone caught between the blades. Bladesurge (Q) refreshes its own cooldown on a Marked target, so E into Q lets you keep dashing and resetting attack-speed stacks through the whole trade.

playing.title: Don't force all-ins past level 6
playing.detail: Once he has R, three stacks of his passive means a free Devour for magic damage with zero cooldown. Fight him down from a poke lead instead of diving a full-health Tahm at three stacks.

playing.title: Push your item-spike window
playing.detail: Your core path hits its stride once Blade of The Ruined King is online around levels 9-13 — use that spike to force skirmishes before his health stacking starts outscaling your current-HP damage.

playing.title: Play for tempo, not a late-game 1v1
playing.detail: The 47.3% head-to-head despite a lane lead means he catches up by late game. Convert your early advantage into plates, drakes, or roams rather than waiting to out-duel a scaled Tahm Kench.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample figures above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the matchup read — timings, trade windows, and the stack/Devour threat — is my own tactical judgment layered on top of the live ability data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being chased by Tahm Kench early game after his (Q) lands. Keep your Conqueror and [P] stacks up to engage.
